question.problem:
$$
{x}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]x,\,{x}_{1}(t)=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t},\,{x}_{2}(t)=[\begin{aligned}t+2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}
$$

Consider the system of linear ODEs and two of its linearly independent solutions ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2},$ shown above. Which of the following is a fundamental matrix for the system?
question.worked_solution:
Given a linear system ${x}^{′}=Ax,$ where $A$ is an $n\times n$ matrix, a *fundamental matrix* $Φ(t)$ of the system is an $n\times n$ matrix whose columns are linearly independent solutions of the system.

In our case, we have a $2\times 2$ system. We are also given that the two linearly independent solutions of the system are the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {x}_{2}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}t+2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}=[\begin{aligned}(t+2){e}^{-t} \\ {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, our fundamental could be written as

$$
Φ(t)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} & (t+2){e}^{-t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}].
$$

**Note:** The columns of $Φ$ can be written in any order.
